bullets.title: October tech/AI rout: semis -17%, Nasdaq worst month since early 2023 AI cycle began
bullets.body: The SOX fell 7.2% on Friday alone and 19.1% from October highs; the Nasdaq suffered its worst monthly decline since the AI cycle began in early 2023 per GS, with the Tech sector down across all subsectors while every other S&P sector was positive. Equal-weight S&P 500 beat cap-weight by 6ppt in October, and 76% of S&P 500 stocks outperformed the index — the largest equal-weight vs. cap-weight gap since April 2009. Mega-cap Growth and Tech underperformed the rest of the market by 11% and 16ppt respectively over three weeks, pushing relative performance to the bottom of long-term trend channel.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle hitting mid-cycle inflection: peak growth, funding concerns, mechanical selling risk ahead
bullets.body: Multiple strategists flagged the AI/tech capex cycle as mid-cycle with revenue and capex growth peaking. Key investor concerns center on fixed income capital availability for AI buildout, PE funding commitment, and chip warehousing costs. The S&P 500 is less than 1% from flipping negative gamma, and UBS's Deleveraging Indicator for ELS Hedge Funds has triggered, with $135-180bn in potential systematic selling leaving the tape vulnerable. GS notes global risk appetite posted its largest drop since November 2021 in October.

bullets.title: Hedge funds flipped underweight AI complex for first time since early 2023; de-grossing at 2018 extremes
bullets.body: Hedge funds moved underweight the AI trade for the first time since early 2023, with the shift primarily reflecting short covering rather than new long additions. Multi-strat de-grossing is now more extreme than late July/early August, near 2018 extremes. US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile as of Oct 29; TMT-focused funds were down 11.9% MTD through Oct 30.

bullets.title: Midterm election week: Democrats 95% to take House, Senate a toss-up; Blue Wave = healthcare/clean energy rotation
bullets.body: Democrats are heavily favored to win the House (95% per Economist model) with the Senate at only 55% Democratic probability. A Democratic sweep is expected to drive sector rotation into healthcare and clean energy, benefit retailers via tariff relief, and support hospital names via Medicaid cut delays. Divided government would keep upward pressure on long-end rates and trigger investigations into Trump-tied corporates; prediction markets put Blue Wave probability at ~66% per JPM.

bullets.title: S&P 500 post-midterm seasonality: 100% hit rate on 6/9/12-month returns since 1990; November historically strongest month
bullets.body: The S&P 500 has risen an average of 15% in the year following midterms since 1950 with a 100% hit rate on 6/9/12-month post-midterm returns since 1990. November is historically the strongest month this century, and the Tech sector has historically been the strongest SPX sector Nov-Jan, outperforming by an average 1.7% since 1990. JPM is tactically bullish on an NDX rebound, noting that 3.5%+ Friday declines historically see ~3% rebounds the following week.

bullets.title: Macro regime: Normal expansion, sticky inflation, Fed hiking in Dec/Mar — below-4% funds rate still accommodative
bullets.body: US real GDP grew 3.4% annualized in 3Q26 with domestic demand surging 6.6%, the fastest in 25 years ex-COVID. The Fed paused at ~4% but multiple strategists (MS, Piper, JPM) expect 25bp hikes in December and March, bringing rates to 4.25-4.5%. Inflation remains sticky with 60% of PCE components rising above 3% annualized; 22V's Macro Regime model shows Normal expansion with unusually high probability, while Hedgeye is positioning for a Quad4 crash pattern.

bullets.title: 3Q earnings: 77-83% beat rate, +30% EPS growth — but guidance revisions turning negative and beats barely rewarded
bullets.body: 60.7% of S&P 500 market cap has reported with 77% beating estimates, aggregate EPS beats of 4.7%, and blended EPS growth of ~30% YoY. However, revenue guidance revisions for 2026 turned negative while EPS remains positive; average downside moves on T+1 post-earnings are 8% vs. 7% upside — the biggest downside skew in 12-year data per Jefferies. 32% of Tech companies posted absolute EPS day moves above 10%.

bullets.title: Cloud acceleration intact: total cloud revenues +58.6% YoY in 3Q; Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48%, AWS +39%
bullets.body: Total cloud revenue reached $117.2B in 3Q26, up 58.6% YoY, accelerating ~9pts QoQ. Google Cloud grew 103% YoY (gaining 200bps share to 26%), Azure accelerated to 48% YoY, and AWS grew 39% with management guiding to 40%+ growth in 2027-2028. Combined Big 4 CapEx reached ~$146B (+$28B QoQ); combined backlogs hit $2.48T. GS raised data center capacity forecasts to 273GW by 2030 from 217GW prior, implying $8.5T capex over 5 years.

bullets.title: Oil -4.5% on Iran diplomacy; GS raises Brent Dec26 to $105, 2027 avg to $88
bullets.body: WTI crude fell ~4.1-4.6% to ~$99.55 on reports of Trump administration pursuing diplomatic resolution with Iran before military action. Despite the near-term pullback, Goldman Sachs raised its oil forecasts: Brent Dec26 to $105/bbl (from $90), 2027 average to $88 (from $80); WTI Dec26 to $94. Copper has also risen ~30% over the past year with a projected ~50% primary supply shortfall by 2040.

bullets.title: Marvell acquires Lumentum for $115B all-stock; creates optical/AI connectivity leader with $550B TAM
bullets.body: Marvell confirmed an all-stock acquisition of Lumentum at a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share, implying ~$1,132/share and a 23.9% premium to the unaffected close, for total enterprise value of ~$115B. The deal is expected to close in H1 2028, be accretive to MRVL non-GAAP EPS in year one, and generate $1B+ in annual cost synergies. The combined company will have a $550B+ TAM; MRVL shares fell ~2-6% and LITE fell ~4% on deal mechanics.

bullets.title: Oracle fires $20B capital raise ($10B equity + $10B debt) alongside Stephens upgrade to $213 PT
bullets.body: Oracle filed a $10B common stock offering (via 424B5) and a $10B debt offering (via 424B2) simultaneously, with shares down ~3% to $130.67 at time of filing. Separately, Stephens upgraded ORCL to Overweight with a $213 PT from $185, implying 63% upside. Microsoft also launched a $25B debt offering on Monday morning.

bullets.title: SpaceX pursuing Boost Mobile acquisition/network deal; telecom stocks T, VZ, TMUS down 2-3%
bullets.body: SpaceX is in talks with EchoStar to either acquire Boost Mobile or use its network, after Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T all declined Musk's requests for network access. The news sent T down 2.3%, VZ down 2.2%, and cable/telco names broadly lower, while ECHO gained ~4%. JPM models SpaceX compute ramping to ~13GW by YE27 with ~$400B ARR exiting 2027.

bullets.title: Value/rotation trade: FCF/EV strongest factor in October (+11%); ex-Tech risk-on factors in Normal expansion regime
bullets.body: FCF/EV was the strongest factor in October at +11%, with investors prioritizing cash generation over earnings beats. Early cyclicals (retail, transports, regional banks), small caps, and equal-weight S&P 500 outperformed by +4.8% to +8% MoM. 22V's Macro Regime model confirms Normal expansion; being short the market is described as difficult as long as that probability remains high, though inflation risk (>0.3% MoM core PCE) would limit upside.

bullets.title: Housing demand collapses: pending sales -15.9% YoY, purchase apps at weakest since Feb 2024 despite rate dip
bullets.body: National median sale price is declining YoY (-0.1%, second consecutive negative print). Pending sales plunged to -15.9% YoY — the weakest since May 2023 — and purchase applications hit -16.8% on a 4-week moving average, the weakest since February 2024. The 30-year mortgage rate fell only 8bps to 7.24%, remaining +107bps YoY at the 97th-percentile level, insufficient to arrest the demand collapse.

bullets.title: META credit outlook cut to negative by S&P on capex/FCF concerns; OpenAI raising only $11B of $30B target
bullets.body: S&P Global revised Meta's credit rating outlook to negative, citing significant uncertainty around capex and free operating cash flow. AI hyperscaler capex is running ~$700B annually with $2T+ projected over two years, creating negative FCF and capital market reliance. Separately, OpenAI is reportedly securing only ~$11B of its $30B funding target at a $1.25T valuation, below the $1.4T target.

bullets.title: Global central banks tightening: ECB, BoJ, BoC, Fed all signaling or executing hikes; 10-year yield at 4.91%
bullets.body: The Fed paused at ~4% but retained above-target inflation concern with two officials voting for an immediate hike; ECB's Lagarde signaled December and March hikes; BoJ held at 1.25% with Ueda calling a December hike 'quite likely'; BoC hiked 25bp to 2.50%. The UST 10-year yield sits at 4.91% — bearish on TRADE per Hedgeye — with a 6% target intact per 22V. JPM recommends 10s/30s curve steepeners.

bullets.title: Semiconductor weakness idiosyncratic to power/infrastructure concerns, not fundamentals — SOX down 19% from highs
bullets.body: JPM identifies the primary semiconductor weakness driver as power/infrastructure concerns and capital availability for AI buildout rather than fundamental demand deterioration. DRAM exports hit a record $34B in October (+595% YoY, 9 consecutive months of 200%+ growth). Evercore sees the server CPU market in the 'first inning' of an agentic AI investment cycle, bullish on INTC and ARM despite PC CPU challenges. 27% of large-cap US stocks had negative realized beta over six months — versus 1.3% long-term average.

bullets.title: Utilities +10% in October vs S&P +0.9% on nuclear/data center PPA wave; power demand forecasts raised sharply
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Utilities Index gained 10% in October, led by nuclear and data center PPA deals: CEG signed a 20-year 890MW nuclear deal with Google, AEP/X-Energy announced 960MW nuclear with Amazon, and NI signed a 20-year Microsoft power agreement. McKinsey raised its data center demand forecast ~25% to 121GW through 2030; GS raised its data center capacity forecast to 273GW by 2030. ENPH fell 16% on a Q3 miss and weak residential solar guidance.

bullets.title: Defense/security supercycle: GS, UBS map $259B opportunity through 2036; humanoid robotics next semi demand driver
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs identifies a structural defense-tech supercycle driven by rearmament, dual-use innovation (drones, distributed power), and geopolitical competition. UBS maps a ~$259B spending opportunity across drones, cyber, space, cloud, and AI through 2036 across 144 companies. Jefferies positions humanoid robotics as the next major semiconductor demand driver, with Melexis engaged with major US/China robotics companies and volumes expected to ramp in the next 12-18 months.

bullets.title: Key earnings this week: AAPL (Mon), AMD/ANET/BKNG/SHOP (Tue), SNAP/EXPE/HUBS (Wed), NET/LYV (Thu)
bullets.body: AAPL reports Monday after close with $113.4B revenue consensus; JPM raised PT to $360 on durable iPhone cycle, expecting ~$56B iPhone revenue (+14% YoY) with ~69M units (-18% YoY) but +20% ASPs. AMD reports Tuesday with $13.1B consensus; ANET reports Tuesday with JPM calling the post-14% pullback a 'favorable setup' for a beat. The earnings calendar represents ~20% of S&P 500 market cap reporting this week.
